scope: Corollary 9.3 (Ordinary cyclic covers along the second Iitaka fibers) of the manuscript “Logarithmic Kodaira dimension and whole-fiber variation” (preprints/Logarithmic-Kodaira-dimension-and-whole-fiber-variation-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b1b750b309e5c5a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 70-71. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In the notation of Propo- sition 9.1 and Corollary 9.2, let J be the generic fiber of x : X′ → W over K = C(W). The LOGARITHMIC KODAIRA DIMENSION AND VARIATION 71 minimal logarithmic generator ω ∈ H0(J, p(KJ + DJ )) is an ordinary regular pluriform. Its resolved connected cyclic root cover e J satisfies H0 ( e J, aKe J ) = Kηa (a ≥ 1), where η is its root top form. In particular, κ( e J) = 0 and h0( e J, Ke J ) = 1. On a dense smooth open of every very general fiber of q : W → U, the family of these covers is geometrically birationally constant with its deck action, and the same holds for the J- family after taking the quotient. More precisely, over the geometric generic q-fiber these families become birational to varieties over bU = C(U) after a finite extension of that fiber’s function field, equivariantly for the deck group in the cover case. These identifications persist under algebraically closed field extension.
